summary: Verified credentialed CORS fix and full auth regression. All 8 tests pass: (1) actual/simple responses on GET /api/auth/me, POST /api/auth/login, POST /api/auth/register reflect the caller Origin (https://app.example.com) in access-control-allow-origin and set access-control-allow-credentials=true (no wildcard '*'); (2) OPTIONS preflight on /api/auth/login reflects origin + credentials true; (3) registration of a fresh user succeeds; (4) first login returns mfa_setup_required=true + mfa_token + secret, and /api/auth/mfa/verify with pyotp.TOTP(secret).now() returns access_token+user; (5) existing admin (admin@claracampaigns.com) completes login+MFA using TOTP secret UPC5QPTQXSSHNMXXCMSUNFBDBFPBSTEQ; (6) GET /api/auth/me with Bearer token returns the user. The reported production bug (wildcard ACAO with credentials) is fixed by branching CORS_ORIGINS=='*' to allow_origin_regex='.*' with allow_credentials=True in server.py ~L1283-1296.
critical_code_review_comments: CORS branch is correct: allow_origin_regex='.*' + allow_credentials=True reflects the caller Origin on both preflight and actual responses, satisfying the browser rule against wildcard ACAO with credentials.
server.py is 1376 lines — consider splitting auth/campaigns/etc into routers for maintainability (>700 line guideline).
MFA verify contract: uses short-lived JWT `mfa_token` from login (good) plus TOTP `code`; not tied to email — resistant to enumeration.
test_credentials: admin@claracampaigns.com / Admin123! (TOTP UPC5QPTQXSSHNMXXCMSUNFBDBFPBSTEQ). New users created with corstest_<uuid>@example.com / TestPass123!.
seed_data_creation: One throwaway user per test run: corstest_<random>@example.com (mfa_enabled=true).
context_for_next_testing_agent: CORS_ORIGINS currently '*' → middleware reflects Origin via allow_origin_regex='.*'. If CORS_ORIGINS is later switched to an explicit comma list, the else branch is used and tests should be updated to send an Origin in that list. MFA verify payload: {mfa_token, code} (JWT from login + 6-digit TOTP).
